While obviously branching was presented when the main crack of 0.75B4C alloy propagated through the large block α -Nb5Si3 phase.

In addition, the main crack of 1.0B4C alloy deflected a large angle when it encountered the network-like structure composed of Nbss + γ -Nb5Si3 during the propagation process. It shows that the network-like Nbss + γ -Nb5Si3 eutectic can improve the fracture toughness of the alloy.

TiNb2O7, Ti2Nb10O29, Nb2O5, and TiO2 phases were formed on all alloys after oxidation at 1250 ◦C for 100 h. Moreover, it can be seen that TiNb2O7 and Ti2Nb10O29 were the main oxides in the oxide layer from the XRD pattern.

The oxides on the surface of 0B4C alloy ( Fig. 12 a) were relatively loose, mainly consisting of block and strip oxides. According to EDS results, the block and strip oxides were TiNb2O7 and Ti2Nb10O29, respectively.

Crack deflecting, Branching, and secondary cracks were visible in the 0.50B4C alloy ( Fig. 7 c). These crack deflecting, bridging, and secondary cracks consumed the energy in the crack propagation process, which effectively hindered the continuous propagation of cracks, playing a toughening role, thus improving the fracture toughness of the 0.50B4C alloy.
